newsitem.title: UK: LEP stronger in Europe with Danish capital.
newsitem.headline: LEP stronger in Europe with Danish capital.

text.p: UK-based global freight forwarder LEP International Worldwide Ltd, part of the LEP Group Plc, announced on Monday that it has invested 25.5 million Danish crowns in re-capitalising LEP International A/S of Denmark.
The investment decision forms part of LEP's current strategy of further strengthening its interests in Europe, particularly in the area of logistics and distribution.
Headquartered in Brondby, LEP International A/S also has offices and freight handling facilities in the major port of Arhus, as well as Padborg.

Around one third of LEP Denmark's revenues are derived from its deepsea operations, one third from airfreight services, and one third from overland trucking and related distribution and logistics activities. Deepsea and airfreight volumes of freight grew by between 15 percent and 20 percent in 1996, and general manager Henrik Dan Larsen is confident of maintaining this level of growth in 1997.

Although the Netherlands is generally recognised as northern Europe's key distribution centre. Denmark is also considered by LEP to be particularly well suited for distribution throughout much of the northern mainland European region.

One LEP speciality is the handling of inbound containers from Asia and the U.S. into Denmark, unloading, picking and sorting, warehousing, and distribution to the Danish market, northern Germany, the Nordic countries and the entire Baltic region.
Using its own trucking network, LEP can deliver to most of these markets within 24 hours.
LEP International A/S also offers a wide range of direct and consolidation airfreight services from and into Kastrup airport.
